title: Nonlinear Localized States on a Pyrochlore Lattice
authors: Faustino Palmero Ramos, Avadh Saxena, Panayotis G. Kevrekidis
abstract: In the present work we explore a prototypical three-dimensional (3d) lattice possessing a flat band in the form of a pyrochlore lattice in the context of a dispersive nonlinear dynamical model, namely the discrete nonlinear Schrödinger (DNLS) equation. We set up the corresponding steady state and dynamical problems and discuss the linear spectrum of the relevant model before delving into a more detailed analysis of the nonlinear equilibria of the system. For the latter, we analyze the more well-established -- at the DNLS level -- fundamental discrete soliton states, as well as vortex structures. For the fundamental solitary waves, we connect their existence and stability with how they approach the linear bands. In the vortex case, we identify their stability features for vortices of topological charge $S=1$ and $S=2$ with those of the honeycomb and triangular lattices. An arguably even more intriguing feature of the pyrochlore lattice concerns the compactly supported nonlinear eigenstates stemming from the flat band of the linear spectrum. These compact localized modes are found to possess oscillatory instabilities for a range of propagation constants in the focusing case, although they can be stable in the latter, while they are found to be subject to symmetry-breaking instabilities in the defocusing nonlinearity case. These results offer a glimpse at the nexus of topology, flat band systems and dispersive nonlinear lattices in three spatial dimensions and as such may be a starting point toward a deeper exploration of such an intriguing interplay.
summary: The paper investigates nonlinear localized states on a pyrochlore lattice modeled by the DNLS equation. It performs detailed stability analyses on solitons and vortices, finding that their stability is strongly dependent on whether the nonlinearity is focusing or defocusing. These results highlight how topology and dispersion govern complex wave behavior in 3D quantum systems.
main_problem: The study explores nonlinear localized states, such as solitons and vortices, on a pyrochlore lattice using a dispersive nonlinear dynamical model.
main_result: The stability of these localized states depends critically on the nonlinearity type (focusing vs. defocusing) and the topological charge of the vortex, revealing complex interplay between topology and dispersion.
method: Stability analysis is performed by linearizing the system around stationary solutions and calculating eigenvalues of the resulting operator, often utilizing the Anti-Continuum limit for theoretical guidance.
model_or_system: The model uses the discrete nonlinear Schrödinger (DNLS) equation on a pyrochlore lattice, which is a 3D structure possessing flat bands in its linear spectrum. This system relates to physical contexts like frustrated magnetism or nonlinear optics.
key_observables: Stability eigenvalues ($\lambda$), topological charge ($S$), and the existence/stability of compact localized modes.
important_parameters: Nonlinearity coefficient ($\gamma$), coupling strength ($C$), propagation constant ($\mu$), and the nonlinearity regime (focusing vs. defocusing).
main_assumptions: The analysis often relies on assuming a standing wave Ansatz and analyzing quasi-two-dimensional configurations, though genuine 3D study is suggested for future work.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the lattice structure, the dispersive/flat bands, and show eigenvalue plots demonstrating stability boundaries as functions of $\mu$ for different state types (solitons, vortices).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from setting up the model on the pyrochlore lattice to analyzing linear spectra, then details the analysis of fundamental solitons and vortex structures, culminating in a detailed comparison of their stability across focusing and defocusing nonlinear regimes.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the interplay between topology (flat bands), nonlinearity, and wave localization in 3D lattices, which is highly relevant for understanding exotic quantum phenomena in optical or magnetic systems.
